title: Aidan didn’t expect a spoken-word component in his thesis - but universities hope it will help tackle AI
summary: Honours students are increasingly being asked to sit oral assessments – but at the University of Sydney it’s become a requirement for all Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast When Aidan Elwig Pollock signed up for an honours program at the University of Sydney, he did not expect his 20,000-word thesis to be accompanied by a spoken component. But, as AI increasingly makes written research an unreliable form of assessment, the university has demanded all students taking the one-year program defend their arguments in conversation with professors. title: The unexpected joy hiding in Grand Theft Auto VI’s chaos? A little routine
summary: Rockstar’s latest blockbuster makes the everyday business of shopping, working out and taking care of a pet snake as compelling as its shootouts and car chases I knew I’d need many skills during the opening hours of Grand Theft Auto VI, but effective time management was not one of them. From playing the previous five titles in the series (and their many spin-offs), I understood I’d have to master Rockstar’s idiosyncratic approach to car handling. True enough, the vehicles do drive like airbeds tied on top of supermarket trolleys. I also knew I’d need to get to grips with the somewhat tricky aiming and shooting if I was to commit any sort of respectable crime spree. But for the first few hours of playing this staggeringly large and bewildering game, what concerned me most was lead character Jason’s personal routine. Each day, he needs to get up, choose an outfit, complete a workout, feed his pet snake Dolores, and perhaps do some DIY, so that when his girlfriend Lucia gets out of jail she’ll fall for him again – rather than fall through his apartment’s rotten staircase. Meanwhile, his drug-smuggling boss phones every five minutes with new parcels for Jason to pick up or drop off, and his pals Cal and Donnie get into all sorts of cocaine-related hijinks they expect Jason to extricate them from. There are also predatory neighbours to do favours for, and groceries to buy. I’ve seen so many people on social media posting about how they took several days off work to play this game, only to find themselves busier and more productive than ever. On his radio show last week, James O’Brien derided himself for completing, in Jason’s apartment, a simple DIY task that he’s put off for months in his own home. I know where he’s coming from. title: Botty? AI helps resurrect voice of John Motson for football video game
summary: Late broadcaster’s family allows EA Sports to create digital version of ‘Motty’ to commentate on popular FC27 First it was Val Kilmer, then Greta Garbo, but finally AI has resurrected a star the terraces can cheer for: John Motson, the BBC football pundit who died in February 2023, is coming back to commentate on the next generation of footballers – at least on a video game. The legendary commentator’s family has approved the use of AI technology to create a digital version of “Motty” – as he was ubiquitously known by generations of football fans – by EA Sports, which makes the popular football simulator FC27. title: ‘It’s been really a mess’: Meta insiders concerned over push to AI content moderation
summary: Several employees say rapid speed at which algorithms work means mistakes can happen at greater scale Meta employees have expressed concern at the company’s push to replace human moderators with artificial intelligence, claiming the technology is leading to mistakes with the potential for sweeping political consequences. The social media company, which owns Facebook and Instagram, has been experimenting with AI-driven moderation for years, first introducing it in 2017 to filter out violent extremist content. title: Which gaming headsets are worth the cost? I put 20 to the test – here are the best for 2026
summary: Wired, wireless, noise cancelling and budget … here are the headphones to level up your PC and console gaming • The best gaming chairs We talk a lot about graphics in video games; we know how important it is to play on a decent screen so we can see what we’re shooting at … or running away from. But what about sound? Explosions, dialogue, the wheezy breathing of a nearby monster – arguably, audio quality is just as important. Many modern games now support 3D or spatial audio, which lets you detect exactly where a sound is coming from in the game world. In survival horror adventures, you can hear the zombie lurking in the next room, and in popular shooters such as Fortnite and Apex Legends, you can pinpoint the footsteps of approaching enemies. title: Amazon to start selling cars in the UK next year
summary: US retail giant links up with Hyundai in attempt to crack £200bn British market Amazon is planning to sell cars in the UK from early next year, in a move that threatens to disrupt the vehicle retail market. The Amazon Autos service will be launched in “early 2027”, starting with cars from the Korean manufacturer Hyundai. It will be the first time the US tech company has sold cars outside its home country. Continue reading...

title: New York bans AI toys, including those using internet to talk to children
summary: The state attorney general says she would ‘not hesitate to enforce’ the five-year ban signed by Governor Kathy Hochul The New York governor, Kathy Hochul , signed legislation on Wednesday that places a five-year ban on the manufacture and sale of toys powered by AI chatbots, including talking stuffed animals, dolls and robots that use the internet to hold conversations with children. The recently re-elected governor, who has also placed a one-year moratorium AI datacenter construction in the state , said that parents shopping for children’s toys “should not have to worry that dangerous chatbots disguised as toys could expose their children to inappropriate conversations, manipulate their feelings or put their privacy at risk”. title: Is grandma asking rude questions at the dinner table again? This Instagram account can help
summary: Life100 features the wisdom of two women in their 80s and has gone viral by exploring important life lessons It is, unfortunately, a familiar scene. At the dinner table, a woman berates her granddaughter with invasive, personal questions – why are you still single? When are you going to have kids? – punctuated by unnerving thrusts of her steak knife. The granddaughter is clearly uncomfortable, but her grandmother pays no attention. Anyone who has been in this situation likely knows what comes next. The granddaughter may try to deflect, only to invite further questioning, or call out her grandmother’s rudeness, which risks escalation. Continue reading...
